title: talent-onramp-squad-10-day-practical-checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a lean, actionable 10-day onramp for squad-level hires (mid-level ICs and junior PMs) intended to get a new joiner to ship a small, measurable outcome and give managers objective signals for continuing investment. Use as a template — swap squad-specific tasks and ownership names.

Why 10 days?
- Short enough to force focused work and quick validation.
- Long enough to observe collaboration, technical baseline, and operational fit.

Structure (high-level):
Day 0 (prestart):
- Invite to Slack, add to team channel and roster.
- Create an initial calendar with 30min 1:1s (Days 2, 6, 10) and daily 15m stand for Week 1.
- Ensure laptop build, access tickets opened: GitHub, JIRA, CI, dev cluster, docs.
- Assign onboarding buddy (not direct manager) and a hiring committee contact for early feedback.

Day 1–2: orientation + tiny-ship task selection
- 1h: team kickoff + 30m practical expectations (what success looks like by Day 10).
- 90m: product walkthrough (must include code-to-prod path or feature-to-customer flow).
- Manager and hire agree on a "Tiny Ship": a scoped change that produces observable output (ex: fix flaky e2e test, add telemetry to a route, small docs-to-prod change).
- Checklist: local dev run verified, test harness passes locally, CI template present.

Day 3–6: execution sprint (pairing + unblock loop)
- Goal: complete Tiny Ship and route a PR for review.
- Pair sessions: at least 3 x 1h pairing blocks with buddy or code reviewer.
- Blocker escalation: maintain a visible unblock issue in JIRA with assignee and SLA (24h).
- Daily: update the "onramp board" column with status: blocked / in progress / ready for review / shipped.

Day 7–8: review, iterate, and documentation
- Address feedback from reviewers and run post-merge smoke tests.
- Draft a short "what I changed and why" blurb for the team email/standup.
- Add a 1-page runbook or README for the change if it touches infra or production config.

Day 9–10: evaluation + next steps
- 30m: hire presents a 10-minute demo + 5-minute Q&A to the squad (focus on decisions, tradeoffs, and remaining risks).
- Manager fills out a compact evidence scorecard (see rubric below).
- Hiring committee sync for calibration if score falls in the amber zone.
- Decide on next-sprint ownership and a stretch goal for the new hire.

Hiring plan fragments (for managers to include in requisition):
- Backfill vs expansion: clearly state whether this role is replacing capacity or increasing scope.
- Must-have skills (2): product-area knowledge, Git-based code review experience.
- Nice-to-have (2): telemetry/observability familiarity, prior infra automation.
- Tiny Ship examples to evaluate practical skills (use for take-home or day 1 assignment):
    - Instrument a route with latency metrics and add tested alerts.
    - Fix a flaky integration test and add a guard to CI to avoid regressions.

Interview rubric (compact, practical, squad-fit focused):
Scale: 1–5 (1: insufficient evidence, 3: meets expectations, 5: strong evidence + stretch)
- Technical baseline (code fluency, debugging): threshold = 3
  - Evidence: ability to walk through a bug, propose a fix, and estimate risk surface.
- Deliverability (PR hygiene, CI knowledge, testing): threshold = 3
  - Evidence: past PR turnaround, test strategy description, CI pain points solved.
- Collaboration (feedback, code review, communication): threshold = 3
  - Evidence: examples of incorporating review feedback and cross-team coordination.
- Ownership & judgement (tradeoffs, scope control): threshold = 3
  - Evidence: decisions that reduced scope/time to value or de-risked launches.
- Systems thinking (observability, incident response): threshold = 2 (nice but not mandatory for some roles)

Interviewer guidance & questions (short list to rotate across interviews):
- "Describe a bug you found in production. How did you investigate and what immediate mitigations did you do?"
- "Walk me through a PR you opened that got pushback. What changed from first review to merge?"
- "How do you decide when to add a test vs when to lean on monitoring?"
- "Give a concrete example of reducing scope to hit a deadline without compromising safety."

Red/Amber/Green decision matrix (quick):
- Green: All thresholds met and at least two 4+ scores. Recommendation: progress to offer or continue with expected ramp plan.
- Amber: At least one threshold = 2 or multiple 3s with mixed feedback. Recommendation: extend trial/onramp (additional 30 days with measurable goals) or request follow-up interview.
- Red: Any critical threshold = 1 or behavioral red flags (team fit, communication breakdown). Recommendation: no hire.

Evidence scorecard (manager to fill):
- Technical baseline: 1-5
- Deliverability: 1-5
- Collaboration: 1-5
- Ownership: 1-5
- Systems thinking: 1-5
- Notes (short): ""
- Recommendation: hire | extend | no_hire

Manager day-by-day checklist (copy into manager's calendar):
- Day 0: confirm access, schedule, buddy assignment.
- Day 1: set expectations, align on Tiny Ship, confirm priorities.
- Day 2: confirm local run and first pairing slot.
- Day 3: unblock check-in, remove blockers or escalate.
- Day 4: review early draft of change, call out missing tests or gaps.
- Day 5: ensure PR draft exists and reviewer assigned.
- Day 6: check CI pass cadence and dev environment parity.
- Day 7: confirm iteration work and docs progress.
- Day 8: rehearse demo with hire, prep reviewers for final pass.
- Day 9: attend demo, collect panel notes.
- Day 10: finalize scorecard and communicate next steps.

Onboarding logistics (fast list):
- Access: confirm SSO, repo, infra console, metrics dashboards, service accounts.
- Communication: add to team calendar, entitlement lists, escalation pager rota.
- Learning: share short list of 3 must-read docs and 2 internal playbooks.
- Tools: confirm accounts for IDE/licensing, local dev images, and deployment keys.

Green/amber triggers for 10-day extension:
- If Tiny Ship is blocked >72h on infra dependencies with no workaround (amber).
- If PR is submitted but reviewer signal is "needs work" across 2 reviewers (amber).
- If continuous miscommunication with teammates or repeated missed syncs (amber/red).

Templates (copy-paste-ready):
- 1-line "Tiny Ship" definition: "Scope: [what], Owner: [name], Success: [observable metric], Risk: [top-1 risk]"
- Interview feedback blurb: "Candidate showed X by doing Y. Main concerns: Z. Suggested next step: [hire|extend|no_hire]"
- Demo intro script: "Today I’ll show the tiny change I shipped that [outcome]. I’ll cover why we did it, how I validated it, and open risks."

Known pitfalls and guardrails:
- Don’t use the Tiny Ship as a vehicle for large migrations — it should be scoped to be completable in the onramp window.
- Avoid conflating ramp speed with role suitability for senior roles; senior hires may need a longer validation period.
- Documentation should not be optional if change affects production runbooks.

Follow-ups (30/60/90 handoff):
- Day 30: manager updates growth plan and assigns first non-trivial ticket.
- Day 60: performance check-in focused on collaboration and shipping cadence.
- Day 90: final onboarding review and leveling calibration.

Notes to people-ops:
- Recommend using this template for hiring requests where outcome measurement is important.
- Track aggregate Tiny Ship completion rate across new hires to refine offer-to-ramp expectations.

End of doc.
